analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/watchdog-isolated-crash-restart.md, lines 1-3) and one new row in the runtime-constants table of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 2206). Both describe a watchdog behavior change, where an isolated crash after a long run is restarted on the next 60 s check. A crash that would continue a crash-loop chain (within 15 minutes of the last restart) still waits the 5-minute grace period. The crash-loop guard threshold of 3 and the update-quarantine/rollback behavior are stated as unchanged. No source code is in the supplied evidence; the cited WatchdogDecision.swift (WatchdogPolicy.graceSeconds) was not supplied, so the behavior is unverified. The doc text itself introduces no secrets, endpoints or controls.

Relevant threat: T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary, TB-003), which concerns the watchdog's restart and rollback authority and availability. Faster restart after an isolated crash could shorten the outage window. It could also let an attacker who can trigger isolated crashes cause more frequent restarts, but the documented chain-continuation grace is intended to preserve the guard. The accompanying Swift change should be reviewed separately to confirm that the chain-detection logic (the 15-minute window and the restart-timestamp/state persistence) cannot be bypassed to defeat crash-loop trip counting or rollback. The cli-reference.md remainder is unchanged context. It includes the logout/token-revocation, drain and add-on documentation, with no new attack surface from this diff. No security regression is identified from the docs alone, and no deeper review is needed for this documentation diff.
